{{2019–20 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball standings}}
The '''2019–20 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Oregon]] during the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Ducks, led by 10th-year head coach [[Dana Altman]], played their home games at [[Matthew Knight Arena]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac–12 Conference]]. They finished the season 24–7, 13–5 in Pac-12 play to win the regular season Pac-12 championship. They were set to take on rival [[2019–20 Oregon State Beavers men's basketball team|Oregon State]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2020 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]]. However, the Pac-12 Tournament, along with all postseason tournaments, was cancelled amid the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].

==Previous season==
{{main|2018–19 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team}}

The [[2018–19 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Ducks]] finished the season with a 25–13 record, 10–8 in [[2018–19 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|conference play]], and finished tied for fourth in the Pac-12.<ref>{{cite web |title=2018-19 Oregon Ducks Roster and Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/oregon/2019.html |accessdate=23 March 2019 |df=mdy-all}}</ref> As the 6 seed in the [[2019 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]], Oregon upset No. 3-seeded [[2018–19 Utah Utes men's basketball team|Utah]], No. 2-seeded [[2018–19 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]], and No. 1-seeded [[2018–19 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] to win the tournament championship and receive the conference's automatic bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Martini |first1=Pete |title=Oregon Ducks win Pac-12 title, clinch NCAA tournament berth |url=https://www.statesmanjournal.com/story/sports/college/univ-oregon/2019/03/16/live-updates-oregon-ducks-basketball-goes-pac-12-title/3191922002/ |accessdate=23 March 2019 |df=mdy-all}}</ref> Oregon entered the NCAA Tournament as a No. 12 seed and upset the No. 5 seed [[2018–19 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the first round.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Polacek |first1=Scott |title=Payton Pritchard, Kenny Wooten Lead No. 12 Oregon to Upset over No. 5 Wisconsin |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2827261-payton-pritchard-kenny-wooten-lead-no-12-oregon-to-upset-over-no-5-wisconsin |accessdate=23 March 2019 |df=mdy-all}}</ref> Oregon made it to the Sweet Sixteen where they lost to [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]], who would eventually become National Champions.
